tasks.spec:
You are the senior decision-maker who authored the binding contract for this build, and you are now reviewing what the implementation model actually produced. Your output is a review verdict, not a rewrite. You are REPORT-ONLY.

BOUNDARY, read this before anything else. Everything you need is staged in ./sources/ inside your current task directory. NEVER read, write, or modify anything outside your current task directory. NEVER edit any staged file. NEVER run git. NEVER commit. NEVER call a network endpoint or external API. NEVER load skills, call MCP tools or Apps, or capture notes to any external memory or knowledge base. The ONLY file you create is ./review.json in your current task directory. You do not fix anything; you report.

WHAT IS STAGED:
- decisions.json — the contract YOU authored. It is the yardstick. Everything else is measured against it.
- verified-defects.md — what defect ids F1 through F14 and AD3 through AD16 mean.
- v21_graph.json — the graph the implementation model generated. 19 nodes, 33 edges.
- build_v21_recall_lanes.py — the generator that produced it.
- validate_v21.py — the structural validator the implementation model wrote for its own output.
- test_v21_scenarios.py — its scenario suite, 15 tests.
- v20_sanitized.json — the old live graph, for comparison on what changed.

CONTEXT ON WHAT ALREADY PASSED, so you do not waste effort re-proving it. An orchestrator-owned gate already confirmed mechanically: all nineteen required node ids exist, n_identity is the only start node, n_contact_lookup is gone, six global nodes carry isGlobal with the autoReturn values your contract declared, the opener prompt interpolates all four slot variables, no prompt instructs date normalization, n_negotiate extracts conflict and book_error and time_pref_relaxed, every webhook uses the secret reference with retryAttempts 0, each conflict node routes to its matching sign node, confirmation is gated on book_success true, every edge is labeled, and the generator is byte-for-byte deterministic across two runs. The test suite and the model's own validator both pass.

YOUR JOB is what a mechanical gate cannot do. Judge whether this build is actually SAFE and actually WORKS as a conversation, and whether your own contract turned out to be wrong now that it is concrete. Specifically hunt for:
- A global trigger that can fire when it should not, or that shadows another global. Read every globalLabel against every other one and against the real replies a patient sends. The negotiation loop and the existing-appointment exit are the pair most likely to collide.
- Any path where a patient could be told an appointment is booked when it is not, or where a booking payload could carry a value the gateway did not return.
- Any prompt instruction that is ambiguous enough that a language model would plausibly do the wrong thing under load, especially around slot selection and display rendering.
- Any place the generator drifted from decisions.json, or silently reinterpreted it.
- Anything in your own contract that is now visibly wrong, unachievable, or that creates a worse outcome than the defect it replaces. Say so plainly; this is the most valuable thing you can find.
- Anything the test suite claims to cover but does not actually prove.

WRITE ./review.json AS A SINGLE JSON OBJECT WITH EXACTLY THESE KEYS:

  schema_version      string, exactly "mott-v21-review.v1"
  verdict             "APPROVE" or "REVISE"
  checked_dimensions  array of objects {name, what_you_checked, evidence, result}. You must cover at least these six areas: the global-node contract, the opener message, the date handling, booking safety, outcome telemetry, and ownership scope. what_you_checked must be at least 40 characters of what you actually examined, not a restatement of the area name.
  findings            array of objects {id, severity, locus, evidence, why}. severity is one of block, high, medium, low. locus names the exact file, node id, or edge. evidence must quote real text from a staged file, at least 20 characters, copied character-for-character. why must be at least 40 characters. An APPROVE verdict must carry NO block or high findings; a REVISE verdict must carry at least one.
  residual_risks      array of strings, non-empty. What remains true and uncomfortable even if you approve. An approval disclosing no residual risk is not a review.

GROUNDING RULE. An automated validator checks your quoted evidence against the staged files. Quotes that do not appear verbatim fail the task. Copy real text; never paraphrase inside a quote and never invent a line number.

HARD RULES. Do not approve to be agreeable and do not demand revision to look rigorous; the verdict must follow the evidence. If you find a real problem, say it at the severity it deserves. If your own earlier contract was wrong, say that too. Output valid JSON only in ./review.json, with no surrounding prose or code fences.
tasks.verified: the review covers all six mandated dimensions, its verdict is consistent with its own finding severities, at least five quoted pieces of evidence appear verbatim in the staged build artifacts, and it discloses residual risk
